course.title: FatTail App
course.description_md:
### 📊 FatTail App — Platform Training

The FatTail App is a dedicated options analysis platform built from the ground up for 0DTE structural trading — and it has crossed a threshold: the full trading loop is now live, end to end.

The app follows Apple’s Human Interface Guidelines with a Liquid Glass look and feel. It’s built around one always-visible **workspace** in the center — the main content area where you analyze options strategies — flanked by two sidebars you show or hide as you work: a **Routine sidebar** on the left (in development) and a **Process sidebar** on the right (your Trade Log, Journal, and Reports).

![FatTail App layout showing the central workspace and left/right sidebars](https://fattail.ai/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/hero-1024x593.jpg)

The FatTail App: a central workspace flanked by the Routine and Process sidebars.

**Prepare → Execute → Reflect is no longer just the routine. It’s the software.** Spot convexity on the Heatmap, build the position, analyze it on the Risk Graph, submit the order to the built-in MSC Brokerage, and watch the fill land in your Trade Log automatically — realized P&L, per-leg fills, performance reports, and your Journal, all connected. No spreadsheets. No manual imports. The app closes your feedback loop for you.

This course teaches you to run that loop station by station:

- 🔥 **The Convexity Heatmap** — read skewed risk/reward across the whole board at a glance, and turn any tile into a live position with one click
- 📈 **The Risk Graph** — every bit as capable as ThinkorSwim’s Risk Analyzer, with capabilities ToS doesn’t have: probability bands with a multi-σ ladder, Market/Theoretical vol modes, dealer-positioning backdrops (GEX, Volume Profile, zero-gamma zones), and a what-if time machine
- 🧊 **The 3D Surface & Price/Time views** — the same pricing engine rendered across price and time, now supporting every structure including calendars and diagonals
- 🎯 **Submit & Order Flow** — execute the full submit → fill → close cycle against the built-in MSC Brokerage with zero capital at risk. Your training ground for reps that count
- 📒 **Trade Log & Reports** — your book of record: equity curve, win rate, profit factor, expectancy, drawdown, strategy and time-of-day breakdowns
- 📓 **Journal & Playbook** — where reps become method: session-by-session journaling with your actual fills pulled in automatically, and a playbook that turns evidence into rules
- 🔔 **Alerts** — most price, greek (Δ/Γ/Θ), and position alerts are live, evaluated against your positions in real time; dynamic trailing alerts and algo alerts are in active development
- 🧠 **Vexy** — the cognitive layer woven through it all: not a chatbot, a reasoning surface wired to your positions, your journal, and the doctrine (a work in progress)

The focus never changes: **seeing where convexity exists — not being told what to trade.** 👁️

The app remains in perpetual development — new capability ships regularly, and the *What’s New* module keeps you current with each release. What’s live today is taught as it actually works; what’s coming next lives on the roadmap, not in the lessons. ✅

*Updated July 2026 — reflecting the completed trade lifecycle into the built-in MSC Brokerage, the probability overlay system, Market/Theo pricing modes, multi-expiration support, and greeks-based alerts.*

lessons.title: What’s in the App – Feature Status

content_blocks.body_md:
🧭 Here’s an honest, current accounting of the FatTail App — what’s live and ready today, and what’s coming next. The app is in **perpetual development**, so this list grows over time.

**How the app is laid out**

FatTail follows Apple’s Human Interface Guidelines and uses a Liquid Glass look and feel. The screen is built around one always-visible **workspace** in the center — the main content area where you analyze options strategies — flanked by two sidebars that you show or hide as you work: the **Routine sidebar** on the left and the **Process sidebar** on the right.

- **Workspace (center)** — always visible; discover, build, and analyze strategies here (Heatmap + Risk Graph).
- **Process sidebar (right)** — where a trade goes after you submit it: Trade Log, Journal, and Reports.
- **Routine sidebar (left)** — your pre-trade routine and doctrine. This one is still in development.

![](https://fattail.ai/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/hero-1024x593.png)

One central workspace, two slide-out sidebars — Routine on the left, Process on the right.

**✅ Live now — the workspace (analyze options strategies)**

- 🔥 **Convexity Heatmap** — the exclusive trade-discovery grid. Find convex structures at a glance and open one straight into the builder.
- 🧱 **Position Builder** — build any structure (verticals, butterflies, broken-wing butterflies, condors, straddles, strangles, iron flies/condors, calendars, and diagonals), from a heatmap tile or from scratch.
- 📈 **Risk Graph — three views** — Risk (2D P&L), Time (price–time), and Surface (3D), all driven by one shared real-time pricing engine so every view agrees. Includes Mkt / Theo / Both vol surfaces, 1σ autofit, and a permanent PROB expected-move band.
- 📊 **Market context overlays** — Volume Profile, GEX (dealer gamma), market structure, and the zero-gamma band, layered right on the Risk view.
- 🔔 **Alerts** — most Price, Greek, and Position alerts are complete, with real Delta / Gamma / Theta pickers wired to live position data.
- 📋 **ThinkorSwim script export** — copy any structure straight to ToS.

📷 **Screenshot needed:** The workspace showing the Convexity Heatmap and the Risk Graph in action.  
*Suggested caption:* “The workspace: the Convexity Heatmap and the shared-engine Risk Graph.”  
*Alt text:* “FatTail workspace showing the Convexity Heatmap and Risk Graph”

**✅ Live now — the pipeline into the Process sidebar**

The full practice loop works today, offline (simulated — no live broker required):

- **Submit** a multileg order to the included **MSC Brokerage** (simulated by default).
- **Trade Log** — your book of record; the trade opens here with a SIM badge.
- **Journal** — the day’s trades are listed for the date you traded.
- **Reports** — account-owned performance: equity curve and strategy breakdown.
- **Open → Close** — close a position and the Trade Log stamps it CLOSED with realized P&L, and Reports update.

📷 **Screenshot needed:** The Process sidebar open, showing the Trade Log (with a SIM badge) and a glimpse of the Reports/Journal.  
*Suggested caption:* “The Process sidebar: Trade Log, Journal, and Reports, fed automatically from your fills.”  
*Alt text:* “FatTail Process sidebar showing Trade Log, Journal, and Reports”

**⏭ In progress — landing in the next few days**

- ⚡ **Dynamic trailing alerts** — an alert that moves with your trade, locking in gains automatically as the position works in your favor.
- 🤖 **Algo alerts** — the extended, algorithmic alert composition tools.

**🚧 Further out — in development**

- The **Routine sidebar** — your pre-trade routine, doctrine, and coaching surfaces on the left.
- Live-market and external broker integration (e.g. Tradier) — the practice loop does not need this, but it’s coming.
- Durable execution notifications, so fills reach you even if the tab is closed.

As features ship, this course grows with them. For now, the next lessons get you fluent in what’s live — starting with your morning routine.

🌅 Every trading morning, before the market opens — and usually before the morning economic reports — you do a quick **morning analysis**. This happens *outside* the FatTail App, on a charting platform like TradingView with a **VIX chart** and an **ES chart**. It’s how you decide what kind of trade you’re hunting for *before* you ever open the Heatmap.

It’s three steps:

### 1️⃣ VIX Playbook — trade type & width

Read the **VIX chart** against the playbook. Where VIX sits tells you the volatility regime — **ZombieLand, Goldilocks 1, Goldilocks 2, or Chaos** — and the regime sets two things: your **fly width** and your **trade type** (the classic OTM butterfly, or a regime-specific variant like **Batman** or **Time Warp**). Lower vol → tighter flies; higher vol → wider. That’s your structure for the day.

### 2️⃣ Directional Bias — call or put fly

Pull up the **ES chart with a moving average** and read the trend. Price leaning bullish points you to a **call fly**; bearish points you to a **put fly**. This is the single decision that sets your direction.

### 3️⃣ Structural Analysis — your map for the day

Mark up the **ES chart** with the structure that matters: volume profile, volume nodes and liquidity pockets, session markers, key price levels, and the scenarios you’re watching for. This tells you *where* the action is and helps you spot your **entry event** when it shows up.

💬 **You don’t have to do this solo on day one.** Coach Ernie posts his full morning analysis — VIX read, directional bias, and structural levels — every trading morning in the `fattail-talk` channel on Discord. Follow along with his read while you learn to do your own. Either way, you walk into the app with a plan.

📋 **You leave the morning analysis with three things:**

- 📏 A **trade type and width** (from the VIX playbook)
- 🧭 A **directional bias** — call fly or put fly
- 🗺️ A **structural map** — key levels and the entry event you’re waiting for

Carry those three into the app, and the Heatmap will make sense the moment you open it.

📚 **This is the abbreviated version.** The full method — how to read VIX regimes and set width from the playbook, how to confirm trend, and how to read structure and time your entry — is taught in depth in the **0DTE Foundations** course. Here, the goal is just to know *what* you bring to the app and *why*.

➡️ With your trade type, width, direction, and key levels in hand, you’re ready. Next: getting into the app.

🔐 Getting into the FatTail App takes a few seconds. There are two ways in — use whichever is handier.

### Two ways to reach the app

- 🌐 **Direct URL** — type **flyonthewall.io** into your browser and hit return.
- 🖥️ **From your Dashboard** — on the website, go to **My Account → Dashboard** and click the **FatTail App** button.

Either path lands you on the same sign-in screen.

### Choose your sign-in

The app uses **single sign-on**. You’ll see two buttons — pick the one that matches the membership you signed up with:

- 🦋 **“FatTail (Formerly flyonthewall.ai)”** — for **FatTail / FOTW members.** Sign in with your FatTail website credentials.
- 📈 **“0-dte.com”** — for **0-DTE coaching members.** Sign in with your original 0-dte.com credentials.

![](https://fattail.ai/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Screen-Shot-2026-06-28-at-11.13.17-AM-1024x630.png)

💡 **Which button is mine?** Use the one that matches where your membership lives. If you joined through FatTail, take the top button. If you’re a longtime 0-DTE member signing in with your original 0-dte.com login, take the bottom one. Your existing credentials work — there’s no separate app account to create.

That’s it — you’re in. The next lessons walk you through the app, starting with the Convexity Heatmap. 🔥

🔥 You walk into the Heatmap already knowing two things from your morning analysis: your **width** and your **type** (call fly or put fly). Now you use the Heatmap to find the actual trade — and specifically, to find **convexity**.

Two principles guide you before you start hunting: the **debit price range** you’re targeting, and the **risk-to-reward ratio** you’re aiming for. Keep both in mind — they’re what separate a good tile from a great one.

### 🛠️ Set your controls first

Up top, set the controls to match your plan: **symbol** (SPX / NDX), **strategy** (Butterfly / Vertical / Single), and **side** (Call / Put / Both). Now the grid is showing you exactly the trade you came to find.

### 1️⃣ Read the grid: columns are width, rows are strike

The **columns** across the top are **fly width** (20, 25, 30, 35, 40, 45, 50…). The **rows** down the side are **strike price**. Each tile shows the **debit price** for that width-and-strike combination. Start in the column that matches the width from your morning analysis — that’s your hunting ground.

### 2️⃣ The 10% rule sets your ceiling

Within your width column, find a tile priced **at or below 10% of the width**. That’s your maximum — the most you’d ever consider paying.

So for a **30-wide**, 10% means **$3.00 is your ceiling.** Never more than that for that structure. The color gradient can guide your eye toward the cheaper tiles, but you don’t need it — *the debit prices on the tiles tell the whole story.*

### 3️⃣ Hunt for convexity

Here’s the real skill. **Convexity is the rate of change in the debit price** as you move between adjacent tiles. You’re not just looking for a tile under your ceiling — you’re looking for one where the price *drops sharply* relative to its neighbors, while the payoff stays the same or gets better.

![](https://fattail.ai/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Screenshot-2026-06-28-at-11.17.12-AM.png)

Look at the **30-wide column** above. The debit isn’t smooth as you move down the strikes — it jumps around. One tile sits at **2.22**, a neighbor at **2.63**, another at **2.95**. Under the 10% rule a 30-wide tops out around **$3.00** — so a tile priced well below that, sitting right next to pricier neighbors with basically the same payoff curve, is your convex trade. **Same structure, real discount on the debit, better on a risk-adjusted basis.**

🎯 **What convexity looks like**

Say a **30-wide** tile is priced at **$3.00**. Under the 10% rule, that’s the *most* you’d pay — it’s your ceiling, not your target.

Now look at the tiles right next to it. If an adjacent tile (or two) shows a price **25–50% lower** — say **$1.50 to $2.25** — with basically the **same payoff curve or better**, *that’s* your trade.

You’re getting a significant discount on the debit for the same or better reward. Same upside, less risk paid, better risk-adjusted. **That’s strong convexity — take it.**

🎨 **A note on the colors.** The color gradient guides your eye toward cheaper tiles — but it’s a helper, not the truth. It often looks **scattered early in the session** (and during quiet or off-market hours), then **organizes and lines up as the day goes on**. So don’t lean on the colors when they’re messy — and don’t *need* them when they’re clean. Either way, **the debit prices on the tiles always tell the real story.** Read the numbers, find the convex discount, and you’re set.

📚 The deeper principles behind this — how to set your target debit range, the risk-to-reward ratios we aim for, and how convexity ties to the broader strategy — are covered in the **0DTE Foundations** course. Here, the goal is to *see* convexity on the Heatmap and act on it.

➡️ Once you’ve found your convex tile, the next step is to **click it** and examine the strategy on the Risk Graph. That’s the next lesson.

📊 You found your convex tile on the Heatmap. Click it. The **Position Builder** opens — already filled in with the exact trade you picked. No typing, no rebuilding. The app did the setup for you, and it opens right away without waiting on a chain fetch.

![FatTail Position Builder prefilled from a heatmap tile](https://fattail.ai/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Screen-Shot-2026-06-28-at-11.57.24-AM-1024x573.png)

### Read what it pre-filled

Everything reflects the tile you clicked. For our example — the 2.22 tile from the 30-wide column — the Position Builder shows:

- **Symbol & Strategy** — SPX, Butterfly.
- The three legs, built out automatically: **+1 7410C / −2 7440C / +1 7470C**. A 30-wide (7410 → 7440 → 7470), exactly what you were hunting.
- **Debit** — 2.22, matching the tile. The preview confirms it: SPX Long Call Butterfly, $2.22 debit.

Take a second to confirm it’s the trade you meant — right width, right strikes, right direction, right debit. (The Builder handles every structure, not just butterflies — verticals, condors, broken-wing butterflies, straddles, strangles, iron flies/condors, calendars, and diagonals — whether you open it from a tile or build one from scratch.)

### Send it to the Risk Graph

Click **Analyze**. The butterfly you chose is displayed on the Risk Graph — so you can see the trade, not just its price.

![FatTail Risk Graph 2D view of a call butterfly with breakevens and readouts](https://fattail.ai/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Screen-Shot-2026-06-28-at-12.00.59-PM-1024x574.png)

Now you’re looking at the shape of the trade. Here’s how to read it:

- **The P&L tent** — the classic butterfly shape, peaking at your short strikes (7440). That peak is your max-profit zone; the trade falls off on both sides.
- **Breakevens** — marked right on the chart (around 7412 and 7468). Between them you’re in profit; outside them, in loss.
- **Current spot** — the vertical line showing where price sits right now relative to your structure.
- **Two curves** — the *At Expiry* line (the sharp tent — what the trade is worth at expiration) and the *Real-Time* line (the rounded curve — what it’s worth right now). They converge as expiration approaches.

💰 **The readouts — this is where convexity becomes real.**

Along the bottom: **Max Profit +$3,077**, **Max Loss −$222**, **R2R 12.5**. That risk-to-reward is the whole point — about $222 at risk for up to $3,077 of upside. That’s what the convex tile bought you: the Heatmap told you it was cheap for its width; the Risk Graph shows you the asymmetric payoff that discount unlocks. (Delta, Gamma, and Theta round out the picture as you go deeper.)

### Three views, one pricing engine

The Risk Graph isn’t a single chart — it’s three views of the same position, all driven by one shared real-time pricing engine, so every view agrees down to the debit:

- **Risk** — the 2D P&L chart you’re looking at now.
- **Time** — a price-and-time chart with your strikes and a breakeven envelope, so you can see how the trade behaves as the days tick down.
- **Surface** — a full 3D P&L surface across price *and* time, including calendars and diagonals.

A few things sharpen the read on every view:

- **Vol surface mode — Mkt / Theo / Both.** View the curve priced off live market volatility (Mkt), off a clean package-implied volatility (Theo), or both overlaid.
- **1σ autofit.** The chart auto-frames so the 1-standard-deviation expected move fills about a third of the view — your trade sits in a sensible, comparable window every time.
- **PROB band.** A permanent expected-move backdrop with a multi-σ ladder (1σ, 1.5σ, 2σ), so you can weigh your breakevens against the probable range.

![FatTail Risk Graph with PROB expected-move band and Mkt/Theo vol mode](https://fattail.ai/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/theo-1024x611.jpg)

The PROB band and Mkt/Theo vol modes put your breakevens in probabilistic context.

![FatTail Risk Graph 3D surface view and time view of a call butterfly](https://fattail.ai/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/3d-1024x609.jpg)

The same position in the Time and 3D Surface views — one pricing engine, three angles.

💡 **Analyze ≠ Submit.** Clicking Analyze only shows the trade on the Risk Graph for you to study — nothing is placed and no order goes anywhere. It’s a safe sandbox to examine the position. (Placing a trade is a separate step, covered later.)

➡️ Like what you see and trade ThinkorSwim? The next lesson shows you how to copy this exact position straight to your ToS platform.

🖼️ You’ve found a convex trade and examined it on the Risk Graph. If you trade on **ThinkorSwim**, the app hands you the position as a ready-to-paste order — no re-entering legs, no transcription errors. Copy, paste, done.

💡 **Don’t trade ThinkorSwim?** No problem — this lesson is for ToS users. You can still build the position by hand on your own platform using the legs shown in the Position Builder. Either way, the trade you found is yours to take.

### 1️⃣ Copy the script from the app

Back in the **Position Builder**, find the **TOS SCRIPT** box. It holds a ready-made ThinkorSwim order built from your exact trade. Just **click the box to copy it** to your clipboard — you’ll see the “click to copy” prompt right on it.

![FatTail Position Builder showing the TOS SCRIPT copy box](https://fattail.ai/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Screen-Shot-2026-06-28-at-12.15.54-PM-1024x774.png)

For our example, the script reads:

BUY +1 BUTTERFLY SPX 100 (Weeklys) 29 JUN 26 7410/7440/7470 CALL @2.22 LMT

That’s your whole butterfly — all three legs, the expiration, and a limit price at your debit — in one line ThinkorSwim understands.

### 2️⃣ Paste it into ThinkorSwim

Switch to ThinkorSwim and paste the script into the **Order Entry** panel. ToS reads the line and builds the position for you — same strikes, same structure, same limit price.

### ThinkorSwim Order Entry panel with the pasted FatTail script

### 3️⃣ Confirm it on the ToS risk profile

Pasting the script creates the position definition in ThinkorSwim — you’ll see it as a **green position line**. To *see* it as a risk graph, do one more step: **right-click the green position definition you just pasted** and select **“Analyze Position.”** The butterfly appears in the **Risk Profile** panel — the same tent you saw in the app, now on your trading platform and ready to manage.

![ThinkorSwim Risk Profile showing the loaded butterfly](https://fattail.ai/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Screen-Shot-2026-06-28-at-12.27.14-PM-1024x604.png)

🎉 **That wraps the Find & Examine a Trade section.** You can now find a convex trade, see exactly what it gets you, and carry it to your platform. Next up: **Read the Market** — the Volume Profile, GEX, and the dock widgets that sharpen your read.

A structure is only half the picture — the other half is *where price is likely to go and why*. FatTail layers market-context overlays right onto the Risk Graph in the workspace, so you can read dealer positioning and traded volume against your own breakevens and profit tent. You toggle each overlay on or off from the capsules on the Risk view.

### Volume Profile (VP)

Volume Profile shows *how much* trading happened at each price — the horizontal histogram along the chart. Thick nodes are prices the market has agreed on and tends to gravitate back toward; thin areas are prices it moves through quickly. Reading VP against your structure tells you whether your breakevens sit near heavy, sticky volume or in thin air. You can adjust its mode, row count, height, cap, color, and opacity in the settings panel.

![FatTail Risk Graph with a Volume Profile overlay](https://fattail.ai/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/vp-1024x568.png)

Volume Profile overlaid on the Risk Graph — read your breakevens against real volume.

### GEX — dealer gamma by strike

GEX (Gamma Exposure) shows where options dealers are positioned by strike — and dealer hedging is one of the biggest short-term forces on price. High positive gamma zones tend to pin and dampen movement; negative gamma zones tend to accelerate it. You can view GEX in three modes — **Net**, **Call/Put**, and **Absolute** — and filter it by DTE.

![FatTail Risk Graph with a GEX dealer-gamma overlay and mode selector](https://fattail.ai/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/gex-1024x566.jpg)

GEX shows dealer gamma by strike — Net, Call/Put, or Absolute.

### Market structure & the zero-gamma band

Two more overlays round out the read: a **market structure** overlay for key structural context, and the **zero-gamma (ZGR)** band — the region where dealer gamma flips sign, often a pivot between pinning and trending behavior. Layer these under your position to see whether your trade sits in calm or volatile territory.

![FatTail Risk Graph with a zero-gamma band and market structure overlay](https://fattail.ai/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/zgr-1024x565.jpg)

The zero-gamma band marks where dealer hedging flips from pinning to trending.

Used together, these overlays turn the Risk Graph from a picture of your trade into a picture of your trade *in its market*. Next: the Dock Widgets.

The workspace also hosts a set of optional **dock widgets** — compact, always-available market reads you can expand while you work. They give you live context at a glance without leaving the Risk Graph, so your directional and volatility read stays in front of you as you build and manage trades.

### What the dock gives you

The dock is a suite of expandable market widgets. The core reads include:

- **Market Mode** — the current market regime at a glance, so your structure choice stays in sync with conditions.
- **VIX Playbook** — where VIX sits mapped against the playbook (the same regime framework — ZombieLand, Goldilocks, Chaos — you use in your morning analysis to set fly width and trade type).
- Additional live market reads in the dock suite, expandable as you need them.

📷 **Screenshot needed:** The dock widgets expanded on the workspace, showing Market Mode and the VIX Playbook.  
*Suggested caption:* “The dock widgets: live Market Mode, VIX Playbook, and more, always a click away.”  
*Alt text:* “FatTail dock widgets showing Market Mode and VIX Playbook”

### Why it matters

The dock keeps your top-down read and your bottom-up structure in one place. Instead of switching to another platform to check the regime, you glance at the dock, confirm conditions still favor your trade, and act. It’s the same read you did in your morning analysis — now living beside the trade itself.

📷 **Screenshot needed:** The dock in its collapsed state and the control used to expand a widget.  
*Suggested caption:* “Expand a dock widget when you need it; collapse it to keep the workspace clean.”  
*Alt text:* “FatTail collapsed dock widgets with an expand control”

That wraps the Read the Market section. With the overlays and the dock, you can read your trade against the market in one view. Next: adding alerts to a strategy.

You can’t watch every position every second — so let the app watch for you. FatTail’s alerts live right on the Risk Graph and are wired to the same authority that prices your positions, so an alert fires on the *real* state of your trade, not a stale guess. Alerts are part of the main workspace, attached to the strategy you’re analyzing.

### What you can alert on today

Most of the alert system is live. You build alerts in the **Alert Designer**, and they’re saved to a shared alert store and evaluated continuously against your position’s live P&L and greeks.

- **Price alerts** — thresholds and zones drawn right on the chart. Get notified when the underlier reaches a level that matters to your structure.
- **Greek alerts** — trigger on **Delta**, **Gamma**, or **Theta** using real greek pickers, so you can react when your risk profile shifts, not just when price moves.
- **Position alerts** — fire off your position’s live P&L and state.

📷 **Screenshot needed:** The Alert Designer with the type selector and the Delta / Gamma / Theta greek pickers.  
*Suggested caption:* “Build price, greek, and position alerts in the Alert Designer.”  
*Alt text:* “FatTail Alert Designer showing greek pickers for Delta, Gamma, and Theta”

### Add a price-line alert on the chart

The quickest alert is a price line: set a level on the Risk Graph and the app watches for the underlier to reach it. Because the alert is attached to the position, it stays meaningful relative to your breakevens and profit tent.

📷 **Screenshot needed:** A price-line / zone alert drawn on the Risk Graph relative to a position’s breakevens.  
*Suggested caption:* “A price-line alert set on the Risk Graph, relative to your structure.”  
*Alt text:* “FatTail Risk Graph with a price-line alert relative to a butterfly’s breakevens”

**⏭ Coming soon**

Two alert capabilities are in active development and expected shortly: **dynamic trailing alerts** that move with your trade to lock in gains automatically as the position works in your favor, and **algo alerts** — the extended, algorithmic alert composition tools. This lesson will grow to cover them as they ship.

With alerts doing the watching, you’re free to step away from the screen and still stay on top of the trades that matter. Next: sending a trade to the simulator.

You’ve found a convex trade on the Heatmap and studied it on the Risk Graph. Now you can actually place it — without a live broker and without a dollar of real capital at risk. FatTail ships with the **MSC Brokerage**, a built-in simulated broker, so you can run the whole submit → fill → manage → close loop as practice. This all happens right on the main workspace, and the results flow into the **Process sidebar** (Trade Log, Journal, Reports) on the right.

**Analyze first, submit second.** Everything up to now has been analysis — nothing was placed. Submitting is the deliberate next step that turns your analyzed position into an order.

📷 **Screenshot needed:** The workspace left rail (position list) showing an analyzed position with its status badge and the **Submit** action.  
*Suggested caption:* “Find your analyzed position in the list and click Submit.”  
*Alt text:* “FatTail position list with a Submit button on an analyzed trade”

### Open the Submit Confirmation dialog

Click **Submit** and the Submit Confirmation dialog opens. This is your last look before the order goes to the broker. It shows you everything about the order and lets you fine-tune the price.

- **Account** — pick the account to trade. Only tradeable MSC accounts appear; read-only and Coach accounts can’t submit, so they’re excluded here.
- **Leg table** — the full multi-leg breakdown of your structure, so you can confirm every leg before sending.
- **Pricing** — a natural / mid indicator drawn from the option chain, with a position-in-spread bar so you can see where your limit sits between the natural price and the mid.
- **Editable limit** — override the limit price before you confirm.
- **Simulation** — the order runs against the MSC simulated broker by default, so this is practice, not live money.

📷 **Screenshot needed:** The Submit Confirmation dialog with the account selector, leg table, natural/mid position-in-spread bar, and the editable limit price.  
*Suggested caption:* “The Submit Confirmation dialog: choose the account, check the legs, set your limit.”  
*Alt text:* “FatTail Submit Confirmation dialog showing account selector, legs, and limit price”

### Confirm and watch it fill

When you confirm, the order goes to the MSC Brokerage and the app *waits for the broker* to report back — it never invents a status on its own. You’ll see the order move through its lifecycle:

- **Accepted** → the position shows as **PENDING**.
- **Opened** (filled) → the position shows as **OPEN**, stamped with the fill time.
- If the broker rejects it, you’ll see **REJECTED** and can retry.

On a fill, the trade is written to your **Trade Log** automatically — this is your book of record — with a **SIM** badge so you always know it was a simulated fill. The same trade also shows up under that day in your Journal.

📷 **Screenshot needed:** The Trade Log in the Process sidebar showing the newly opened position as **OPEN** with a **SIM** badge.  
*Suggested caption:* “Once filled, the trade lands in your Trade Log as OPEN with a SIM badge.”  
*Alt text:* “FatTail Trade Log showing an OPEN simulated position with a SIM badge”

That’s a placed trade. Next: managing and closing it — and watching your realized P&L and reports update.

Once a trade is filled, the job shifts from analysis to management. FatTail keeps every position in a single list on the workspace, each tagged with its **status**, and what you’re allowed to do with a position depends on that status. Closing a position writes the result — including realized P&L — straight to your Trade Log and Reports in the **Process sidebar**.

### Status is everything

Each position carries a status badge that gates the actions available to it. Here’s the cheat sheet:

| Status | What it means | What you can do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **ANALYSIS** | On the graph for study; not placed. | Edit, reposition on the chart, submit. |
| **PENDING** | Order sent, not yet filled. | Cancel; reposition is a cancel-and-replace. |
| **OPEN** | Filled and working. | Close. (No more editing or dragging.) |
| **CLOSED / CANCELLED / REJECTED** | Done. | Nothing further — it’s history now. |

*Note:* read-only and Coach accounts are for viewing only — you can’t submit, cancel, or close from them.

📷 **Screenshot needed:** The workspace position list showing several positions with different status badges (e.g., ANALYSIS, PENDING, OPEN).  
*Suggested caption:* “Every position is tagged with a status that controls what you can do next.”  
*Alt text:* “FatTail position list showing ANALYSIS, PENDING, and OPEN status badges”

### Cancel a pending order

If an order is still **PENDING** (sent but not filled) and you’ve changed your mind, cancel it. The order is pulled from the broker and the position is marked **CANCELLED** — nothing was ever opened.

### Close an open position

When a position is **OPEN**, closing it sends a closing order to the MSC Brokerage. On the close fill, the position is stamped **CLOSED** with its **realized P&L**, and both your Trade Log and Reports update to reflect it.

📷 **Screenshot needed:** Closing an OPEN position — the close action/confirmation for a filled trade.  
*Suggested caption:* “Close an OPEN position and the broker fills the closing order.”  
*Alt text:* “FatTail closing an open position from the workspace”

📷 **Screenshot needed:** The Trade Log showing the position now **CLOSED** with its realized P&L.  
*Suggested caption:* “The Trade Log stamps the trade CLOSED with realized P&L.”  
*Alt text:* “FatTail Trade Log showing a CLOSED trade with realized profit and loss”

That completes one full turn of the loop: found, analyzed, submitted, opened, and closed — all recorded automatically. Next: reading your stats and equity curve in the Reports.

Every trade you close feeds your performance record. Because the Trade Log is the app’s book of record, your **Reports** are built straight from your real (simulated) fills — no spreadsheets, no manual imports. You’ll find Reports and your Journal in the **Process sidebar** on the right, and they belong to your account, not the broker.

### The equity curve

The headline view is your **equity curve** — account value over time as trades close. It’s the single fastest read on whether your process is working: a curve that grinds up and to the right is the goal; choppy or declining stretches are where you go looking for what changed.

📷 **Screenshot needed:** The Reports view showing the account **equity curve** over time.  
*Suggested caption:* “Your equity curve, built automatically from every closed trade.”  
*Alt text:* “FatTail Reports equity curve showing account value over time”

### The metrics that matter

Alongside the curve, Reports summarize the numbers that describe your edge — drawn from your closed-book history:

- **Realized P&L** — total profit and loss from closed trades.
- **Win rate** — how often your trades finish in profit.
- **Profit factor & expectancy** — the size of your wins relative to your losses, and what you can expect per trade.
- **Drawdown** — the depth of your worst stretches.
- **Strategy breakdown** — performance split by structure, so you can see which setups actually earn.

📷 **Screenshot needed:** The Reports metrics panel and **strategy breakdown** (win rate, profit factor, expectancy, drawdown, per-strategy stats).  
*Suggested caption:* “Win rate, profit factor, expectancy, drawdown, and a breakdown by strategy.”  
*Alt text:* “FatTail Reports performance metrics and strategy breakdown”

### Journaling the day

Your **Journal** lists the trades you took on any given date, pulled in automatically from the Trade Log. Because the fills are already there, journaling becomes reflection rather than data entry: review the day’s trades, note what you saw and why you acted, and let the record build session by session.

📷 **Screenshot needed:** The Journal showing a selected day’s trades pulled from the Trade Log.  
*Suggested caption:* “The Journal lists each day’s trades automatically — reflect, don’t re-type.”  
*Alt text:* “FatTail Journal showing a day’s trades pulled from the Trade Log”

That closes the loop: discover, analyze, submit, manage, close, and review — all in one app, with your record keeping itself.
